_portCommentC6: ESP32-C6 (M5NanoC6) port under ports/m5stack_riscv (vendored at stage 1, commit 709b36a; file-by-file record in ports/m5stack_riscv/runtime/IMPORT_PROVENANCE.md; stages 2-4 added the wifi-connect runtime, DNS and the M5NanoC6 board, docs/c6-port.md): its provenance is the PRIVATE development repository directly, the same way the wpa2 archives under ports/m5stack_xtensa/runtime/wifi/prebuilt/wpa2 record theirs, because the public snapshot fdd89f8 named above contains no C6 at all (fmp3/arch/riscv_gcc holds esp32p4 only). Replace portBaseRepositoryC6 / portBaseCommitC6 with the public repository and its snapshot #8 commit once that snapshot is published; until then this is the only commit the C6 sources can be compared against. The two commits the C6 provenance records name the SAME sources: portBaseCommitC6 (c7fef18) is what the port and the four prebuilt archives were taken from, and the lwIP archive's README also names 5bdac26e, which is only the dev tree's HEAD on the day that archive was rebuilt with LWIP_DNS 1 (stage 4) - the script, the lwIP sources and the port files it reads are unchanged between the two. What the release carries for the C6 board is the same shape as for the Xtensa boards, and the entries below are chip-neutral on purpose: the runtime SOURCES under ports/m5stack_riscv are not distributed (no ports/ source of any chip is; the platform archive carries prebuilt stages, fmp3-prebuilt/<chip>/<profile>, and the bundled library), the four prebuilt archives under ports/m5stack_riscv/runtime/wifi/prebuilt/{wpa2,lwip}/esp32c6 (Git-tracked, with their READMEs and licenses beside them) reach the user only inside the esp32c6/wifi-connect stage's lib/, and every example is shared across the boards - the examples a C6 profile is verified with are scripts/verify_package.py BOARD_PROFILES x PROFILES. scripts/capture_c6_usj.sh (the development-side flash-and-capture script) is not distributed, like everything else under scripts/. Which stages and which M5Stack tools the C6 board requires is releaseArtifacts.platformArchive below.
_portCommentC5: ESP32-C5 (M5Stamp-C5) port, a chip branch of ports/m5stack_riscv beside the C6 (plan 4 A2: arch/riscv_gcc/esp32c5, target/m5stampc5_gcc, config/esp32c5, seam/seam_c5_*, cmake/prebuilt_stage_c5.cmake, toolchain-riscv-esp32c5.cmake, and the newly written arduino/arduino_gpio_c5.c and arduino/arduino_interrupt_c5.{c,cfg,h}; file-by-file record in ports/m5stack_riscv/runtime/IMPORT_PROVENANCE.md and IMPORT_PROVENANCE_c5.md beside it): its provenance is the PRIVATE development repository directly, the same way portBaseCommitC6 above records the C6, because the public snapshot fdd89f8 named by portBaseCommit contains neither chip. portBaseCommitC5 (1d96bcba) is the commit that ends the development side's C5 plan 3, and it is what both the port sources and the four prebuilt archives under runtime/wifi/prebuilt/{wpa2,lwip}/esp32c5 were taken from. Replace portBaseRepositoryC5 / portBaseCommitC5 with the public repository and its next snapshot commit once that snapshot is published; until then this is the only commit the C5 sources can be compared against. Stages 1-4 built the chip branch, the m5stampc5_fmp3 board and the minimal / wifi-connect stages and exercised them on hardware (docs/c5-port.md: Blink warm 5/5 and true-cold 5/5 at stage 2; at stage 4 a Wi-Fi scan covering 2.4 and 5 GHz, STA -> DHCP -> DNS -> TCP warm 3/3 and true-cold 3/3 - the association was WPA3-SAE, WPA2-PSK alone is unmeasured - and the self-driven attachInterrupt test). What the release carries for the M5StampC5 board has the same shape as for the other four boards, and the entries below stay chip-neutral on purpose: the runtime SOURCES under ports/m5stack_riscv are not distributed (no ports/ source of any chip is; the platform archive carries prebuilt stages, fmp3-prebuilt/<chip>/<profile>, and the bundled library), the four prebuilt archives under ports/m5stack_riscv/runtime/wifi/prebuilt/{wpa2,lwip}/esp32c5 (Git-tracked, with their READMEs and licenses beside them) reach the user only inside the esp32c5/wifi-connect stage's lib/, and every example is shared across the boards - the examples a C5 profile is verified with are scripts/verify_package.py BOARD_PROFILES x PROFILES. scripts/capture_c5_usj.sh (the development-side flash-and-capture script) is not distributed, like everything else under scripts/. Which stages and which M5Stack tools the C5 board requires is releaseArtifacts.platformArchive below (prebuiltStages.esp32c5, chipToolDependencies.esp32c5: esp-rv32 2601 and esp32c5-libs 3.3.9), added at stage 1 together with the tables scripts/test_check_release_artifacts.py holds them against.
_portCommentP4: ESP32-P4 (M5Stamp-P4) port, a chip branch of ports/m5stack_riscv beside the C6 and C5 (StampP4 plan stage A1: arch/riscv_gcc/esp32p4, target/m5stamp_esp32p4_gcc, seam/seam_p4_*, cmake/prebuilt_stage_p4.cmake, toolchain-riscv-esp32p4.cmake, app/phase3_p4; file-by-file record in ports/m5stack_riscv/runtime/IMPORT_PROVENANCE_p4.md). Its provenance is the PRIVATE development repository directly, like the C6 and C5 rows: portBaseCommitP4 (a7453186) is the dev main commit the P4 layer was copied from - the layer itself was last changed there in August 2026 (the seam-p4-smp preset, booted on the M5Stamp ESP32P4 rev v1.3 hardware at dev stages 2-6; hosted Wi-Fi at stages 7a-7g on the Tab5). Replace portBaseRepositoryP4 / portBaseCommitP4 with the public repository and its next snapshot once published. What the release carries for the M5StampP4 board has the same shape as for the other boards: the runtime SOURCES under ports/m5stack_riscv are not distributed, the esp32p4/minimal stage is (fmp3-prebuilt/esp32p4/minimal), and every example is shared across the boards. minimal at stage A; wifi-connect was added at stage B and is HOSTED - the P4 has no radio of its own, so that stage carries the SDIO host, the esp_hosted transport and RPC, the 802.3 data path and lwIP, and the radio is a companion ESP32-C6 on the Stamp add-on (vendored under ports/m5stack_riscv/runtime/hosted, recorded in IMPORT_PROVENANCE_p4.md sections 5-8; the prebuilt lwIP archive runtime/wifi/prebuilt/lwip/esp32p4/liblwip.a reaches the user only inside that stage's lib/, like the C6's and C5's). The board has no display, so no m5-unified, and no BR/EDR radio, so no bt-classic. The SDK the stage is built against is esp32p4_es-libs (chipToolDependencies.esp32p4), the pre-v3-silicon variant that the M5Stack core's m5stack_stamp_p4 row selects by default; the board's ChipVariant menu is dropped by install_platform.py so that a sketch cannot be linked against the other variant's ROM scripts. The board was added without hardware at hand (stage A1-A3 are compile / link / X-check only; stage A4 is the hardware run on another machine).

entries._comment: the dual-core profile is gone (m5-unified now builds the SMP kernel), and a shipped stage has no PRC2 task, so this example cannot demonstrate anything a user could reproduce. It stays in the repository as the input to Test-Smp.ps1, which builds it against phase6_smp_selftest. Ship it again once sketches can place their own task on PRC2.

M5Core only: the ESP32-S3 has no BR/EDR radio, so the CoreS3 and StickS3 boards have no Bluetooth Classic (SPP) runtime option. It ships anyway, because packaging/README.release.md points users at this example by name and the three boards share one architecture - Arduino cannot offer a library example for one board out of three. The example itself refuses to compile on the other two with a sentence saying which board to pick, rather than failing at the link.

a test fixture, not something to hand a user: it deliberately never calls M5.begin(), because it exists to prove that an Arduino-compiled object can take the address of the FMP3-linked M5 and be linked into the image. Test-M5UnifiedLink.ps1 builds it and Test-Hardware.ps1 flashes what that produces. Listed here with boardsManager false, the same way DualCore is, so that its absence is a statement rather than an omission - make_package_index.py now rejects an example that appears in neither.

a teaching sample, not a self-test: it draws a face with M5GFX primitives and reacts to touch, so a beginner has something to modify. It calls toppers_m5_begin() rather than M5.begin() because this port implements no GDMA and the adapter is what clears the panel's DMA channel. It has no sound - the m5-unified profile excludes Speaker_Class.cpp and begins with internal_spk false - and playHappySound() says so in place of a tone.

M5NanoC6 only (stage 6): pinMode/digitalWrite/digitalRead, a self-driven attachInterrupt test and the RGB LED, all provided by the ESP32-C6 wifi-connect runtime. It ships to every board for the same reason BluetoothSPP does - one architecture-neutral library, four boards - and is guarded with ARDUINO_M5STACK_NANO_C6: on the three Xtensa boards it compiles and links to a setup() that logs one line saying which board it targets, instead of failing at the link with an undefined rgbLedWrite (the Xtensa boards have no RGB LED driver). The README.md beside it is repository documentation (what the example tests and which log lines to count) and is not distributed: the platform archive carries the .ino named here only.

M5AtomS3 Lite only (2026-09-17): its on-board WS2812B-2020 RGB LED on G35, driven by the ESP32-S3 wifi-connect runtime's rgbLedWrite (ports/m5stack_xtensa/runtime/arduino/arduino_rgb_led.c, the ESP32-C6 driver ported to this chip). It ships to every board for the same reason NanoC6Gpio does - one architecture-neutral library, six boards - and is guarded with ARDUINO_M5STACK_ATOMS3LITE, a macro this package makes: install_platform.BOARD_BUILD_OVERRIDES rewrites the build.board the row inherits from m5stack_atoms3, which is the LCD-bearing AtomS3 and a different device. On the other five boards it compiles and links to a setup() that logs one line saying which board it targets; without the guard the link fails on the M5Core and the M5StampC5 with an undefined rgbLedWrite (measured). The README.md beside it is repository documentation and is not distributed.

M5AtomLite only (2026-09-17): its on-board SK6812 RGB LED on G27, driven by the ESP32 wifi-connect runtime's rgbLedWrite (ports/m5stack_xtensa/runtime/arduino/arduino_rgb_led_lx6.c, the ESP32-S3 driver ported to the LX6). It ships to every board for the same reason AtomS3LiteRgb does and is guarded with ARDUINO_M5STACK_ATOM, the build.board the row inherits unchanged from the M5Stack core's m5stack_atom (the ATOM Lite / Matrix / Echo share that row upstream). On the other six boards it compiles and links to a setup() that logs one line saying which board it targets; it also carries a runtime guard, because the M5AtomLite offers Minimal and Bluetooth Classic (SPP) as well and neither links the driver. Link-verified only when added (no board at hand); the README.md beside it is repository documentation and is not distributed.

Every board (2026-09-15): pinMode/digitalWrite/digitalRead and a self-driven attachInterrupt test, now that the Xtensa runtime has arduino_gpio.o too (m5-unified / wifi-connect / bt-classic; minimal has neither). The probe pin is chosen per board define (M5NanoC6 G7, CoreS3 G8, M5Stack Basic G16, M5StickS3 G9, M5StampC5 G1, M5AtomS3 Lite G7; all six verified on hardware, the last one 2026-09-17; M5AtomLite G23, link only until that board is run). Its README.md is repository documentation and is not distributed.

_releaseArtifactsComment: a release is three kinds of artifact, not one. The platform archive carries the board definition, the prebuilt stages and the bundled library; the link driver is a separate Arduino tool frozen once per host, because a sketch build needs it and no package index ships a Python interpreter. scripts/check_release_artifacts.py verifies an assembled release against this section before it is published.

platformArchive._prebuiltStagesComment: chip -> the prebuilt stages (fmp3-prebuilt/<chip>/<profile>/link-manifest.json) the archive must hold for every chip it ships a board for. A chip present in the archive with a profile missing here, or a chip the archive holds that has no row, fails check_release_artifacts.py. A chip in this table that the archive does not hold at all is reported, not failed: whether a chip ships is decided by which stages install_platform.py was given. The same table as the stage check in .github/workflows/verify-package.yml and EXPECTED_PROFILES in scripts/install_platform.py. esp32c5 offers the same pair as esp32c6 since C5 plan stage 3 (docs/c5-port.md); the drift test holds this row against the other tables.
platformArchive._chipToolDependenciesComment: chip -> M5Stack tools the current platform entry's toolsDependencies must name whenever the archive holds that chip's stages (R9 of the C6 plan). The Xtensa tools are unconditional in the index and are not listed here; the RISC-V toolchain and the ESP32-C6 / ESP32-C5 SDKs are declared by make_package_index.py only when fmp3-prebuilt/<chip> is packaged, so that a release without those boards does not make every user download them - and this row is what catches the gate silently ceasing to fire while the stages still ship. esp-rv32 is shared by the two RISC-V chips and appears once in the index. The values mirror CHIP_TOOL_DEPENDENCIES in scripts/make_package_index.py; scripts/test_check_release_artifacts.py holds the two together.

linkDriver._hostsComment: Arduino host triplets a release must carry a frozen driver for. x86_64-apple-darwin is absent on purpose: the macos-13 runner stopped being allocated, and a queued job hangs rather than fails, so it would stall the release. Intel Macs cannot build with 0.3.0. Add the host back here and in both workflows once a working Intel label exists.
